It asks for 35,000 of your 45,000 monthly surplus, which leaves you 10,000 of breathing room each month. Out of 10,000 simulations run on real historical market returns, 8,700 reached your goal. It also held up against every combination of shock events we tested.

goal_priority_note: Your house downpayment is funded first because it is five years away, while the child education goal is twelve years out and can absorb a slower start. The nearer deadline is the binding one, so it sets the monthly figure.
mismatch_note: You described your approach as aggressive, but your transaction history looks moderate. On two occasions you sold equity within days of a market fall. That matters here because the plans with the highest projected returns are exactly the ones that fall furthest during a bad year, and a plan left early performs worse than a slower plan held to the end.
